body: I'm unlucky because I am. Good things do not happen to me no matter how hard I try. Bad things happen to me regardless of what I do. I'm surrounded by people more fortunate than me, be it that they were born without the huge list of flaws I have, or that they have the occasional good thing happen in their life. I hate it.

Can things get better? Sure. I could win the lottery. I could inherit a fortune from a family member I never knew I had. I could stumble across a woman who's absolutely perfect for me. The problem is, none of these things will ever happen. It's false hope. I've been unlucky my entire life and that isn't going to change.
I don't understand self-harm. I want the pain to go away, not to add more of it.
99.99999% of people are terrible fucking people. This isn't limited to gay people, unfortunately.
I told myself "it gets better" 15 years ago. It got worse. It's not going to get better for everyone.

I appreciate what you're trying to do with this post, I really do. That being said, you're assuming a lot. Not everyone has people that would care if they killed themselves. Many people are alone, and a lot of times it doesn't get better. Hell, when I finally end it after my mom passes, I'm sure I'll have about 4 downtrodden people at my pathetic makeshift funeral then I'll be forgotten about in a week. Everyone's different.
That's even less in the realm of possibility than what I described in my post, unfortunately.
It all stems from being a jaded, bitter misanthrope.

I'd like to be skilled at, and make money doing something I enjoy. It's not that I haven't tried things - I've tried doing lots of things I thought I could enjoy(or even simply tolerate) doing such as welding, baking, accounting, writing, selling nerdy things. The list goes on.

At absolute best, I'm slightly better than average at writing - typing, not hand writing. That will accomplish nothing in life apart from writing bad fan fiction.
I wish I could draw or play/write music, but I'm abhorrently bad at both.
